eyebrow: The EU AI Act's risk pyramid (real, enacted law)
code:
Unacceptable risk -> banned outright
                     (e.g. social scoring by public authorities)

High-risk         -> conformity assessment, human oversight,
                     technical documentation (HR, credit, infra)

Limited risk      -> transparency obligations
                     (disclose it's AI; label AI-generated content)

Minimal risk       -> no additional obligations
caption: Obligations scale with risk tier — not every AI system is regulated the same way.

eyebrow: The standard you can be audited against
code:
ISO/IEC 42001 = AI management system standard
(the AI counterpart to ISO/IEC 27001 for infosec)

  - documented policies & defined roles
  - risk assessment processes
  - continual improvement
  - independently certifiable

AI governance board reviews each system against:
  EU AI Act tier + NIST RMF evidence + ISO 42001 docs
caption: Voluntary guidance, binding law, and a certifiable standard — three different kinds of real governance.
